entry.title: Website monitoring for small business: what to check first
entry.summary: How small businesses can watch important website pages, SSL certificate expiry and incident/recovery email alerts, with limitations and a practical checklist.
entry.content: Start with your homepage, contact or enquiry page, and customer booking page. Website monitors flag HTTP response failures and, where configured, missing page text. Check alerts from a second source before assuming a widespread outage. Learn the fundamentals and explore SiteGuard, a ClientStream service, at the linked guide.

entry.title: Website down? A small business outage response checklist
entry.summary: Verify a website outage, identify likely causes, communicate carefully and confirm recovery without unnecessary configuration changes.

entry.title: SSL certificate expiry: what to check
entry.summary: Practical HTTPS certificate health and renewal checks for small businesses, including the limitations of basic uptime monitoring.

entry.title: Website down? A practical small-business response checklist
entry.summary: Confirm a website outage from another network, check hosting, DNS and TLS, communicate carefully and verify recovery.
entry.content: The most important response to a business website outage is to confirm it, preserve error details and locate the failing component before making changes. This guide gives practical DNS, hosting, certificate and post-recovery steps, with a clearly labelled optional SiteGuard monitoring service.

entry.title: SSL certificate expiry checks for a small business website
entry.summary: What an HTTPS expiry warning means, how to investigate failed renewal, and how to check business websites.
entry.content: Expiry, incorrect hostnames, incomplete chains and deployment of old certificates can all trigger security warnings. Inspect the public certificate and validation/renewal setup before visitors are affected. Learn the practical checks and limitations of single-location SSL visibility.
